# README.md

# kaboo-react

> React components + hooks for rendering kaboo multi-agent activity in a
> [CopilotKit](https://copilotkit.ai) app, with batteries-included CopilotKit
> integrations.

[![npm version](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/kaboo-react.svg)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/kaboo-react)
[![license](https://img.shields.io/npm/l/kaboo-react.svg)](./LICENSE)
[![docs](https://img.shields.io/badge/docs-mkdocs-blue.svg)](https://gl-pgege.github.io/kaboo-react/)
[![CI](https://github.com/gl-pgege/kaboo-react/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/gl-pgege/kaboo-react/actions/workflows/ci.yml)

kaboo-react renders a live, hierarchical view of what your agents are doing —
sub-agent cards, tool calls, streamed tokens, structured outputs, drill-down
navigation, questions and approvals. Sub-agents ride the **same AG-UI run
stream** as the chat, as AG-UI's own `SUBAGENT_*` events, so there is no separate
endpoint to wire up: kaboo-react is a batteries-included CopilotKit plugin.

## Features

- **Live hierarchical activity** — nested agent/tool cards that stream in as work
  happens, inside the chat transcript, with what needs the person lifted into
  the main chat under the agent's name.
- **Drill-down navigation** — breadcrumb + detail view to explore any sub-agent.
- **Questions and requests** — `useAskUserTool` and `useRequestTool` register
  the browser's tools, with arguments checked against their schema.
- **Approvals** — on CopilotKit's `useInterrupt`, with N parallel requests
  resolved independently, remembered scopes and deadlines.
- **Canvas hooks** — `useAgentState`, `useLiveToolCalls` and `useAgentPresence`
  let a canvas follow the agents.
- **Generative UI** — A2UI, Open Generative UI and MCP Apps pass through to
  CopilotKit, with sub-agents' surfaces labelled.
- **Structured renderers** — plug custom UI for schema-shaped agent output.
- **References & attachments** — files and your own objects (tables, dashboards,
  …) as interactive inline chips, added from one shared **+** / **@** popover.
- **Batteries included** — one `KabooProvider` renders `<CopilotKit>` and mounts
  every context and handler for you.
- **Themeable** — styled with CSS variables and `--kaboo-*` tokens.

## Install

```bash
yarn add @pgege/kaboo-react
```

Peer dependencies: `react`, `react-dom`, and `@copilotkit/react-core` (>= 1.79.1).

Import the stylesheet once, near your app root:

```ts
import "@pgege/kaboo-react/styles.css";
```

## Quick start

`KabooProvider` renders `<CopilotKit>` for you and mounts every kaboo context and
handler inside it. Give it the runtime URL, the entry agent, and a thread id —
then drop in the components.

<!-- source: examples/minimal/src/App.tsx#quickstart -->
```tsx
import { CopilotChat } from "@copilotkit/react-core/v2";
import { KabooProvider, GlassTabs, DrillDetailView } from "@pgege/kaboo-react";
import { KabooMessageView } from "@pgege/kaboo-react/copilotkit";
import "@pgege/kaboo-react/styles.css";

export function App({ agent, threadId }: { agent: string; threadId: string }) {
  return (
    <KabooProvider runtimeUrl="/api/copilotkit" agent={agent} threadId={threadId}>
      <GlassTabs />
      <CopilotChat messageView={KabooMessageView} />
      <DrillDetailView />
    </KabooProvider>
  );
}
```

That's it — `KabooProvider` renders `<CopilotKit>` and nests kaboo's contexts
(`KabooActivityProvider`, `DrillProvider`, the renderer registries) plus the
built-in `KabooInlineCards` and `KabooInterruptHandler`. It passes
`properties`, `renderToolCalls`, `renderActivityMessages`, `a2ui` and
`openGenerativeUI` through to CopilotKit. Disable the auto-mounted handlers with
`disableInlineCards` / `disableInterruptHandler`, and forward any other
CopilotKit props via `copilotKitProps`.

## Core concepts

- **Sub-agents ride the run stream.** The backend streams them as `SUBAGENT_*`
  events with their tagged text and tool calls, on the same AG-UI run stream as
  the chat. `KabooActivityProvider` folds them into groups and exposes them via
  `useActivity()`, live and on replay alike.
- **Providers nest under `KabooProvider`.** Activity → drill → renderers, with
  the built-in handlers mounted inside.
- **Two barrels.** Import framework-agnostic pieces from `kaboo-react`, and the
  CopilotKit-coupled integrations from `@pgege/kaboo-react/copilotkit`.
- **The `threadId` scopes everything.** Each conversation gets its own
  hierarchical activity view automatically.
- **Theming via CSS variables.** Components read standard design-system tokens and
  accept `--kaboo-*` overrides.

## References & attachments

Let users attach things to a message. Everything is driven by **reference
providers** registered on `<KabooProvider references={…}>` and rendered by the
`KabooReferenceInput` slot. There are two transports:

- **Attachment** — a file/blob. Register the built-in `uploadProvider({ onUpload })`;
  choosing "Attach a file" (from **+** or **@**) opens the picker, uploads, and
  drops a file chip inline. Files ride the message as parts stamped with
  `kaboo_id` / `kaboo_kind` / `kaboo_name`.
- **Object** — a pointer to one of *your* entities (`table`, `dashboard`, …).
  Register a `ReferenceProvider`; selected objects sync into
  `state.kaboo_references` for the backend to resolve, and appear inline as
  `@name`.

```tsx no-verify
import {
  KabooProvider,
  KabooReferenceInput,
  uploadProvider,
  type ReferenceProvider,
} from "@pgege/kaboo-react";

// A custom object reference: three fields make it work.
const tableProvider: ReferenceProvider = {
  id: "table",
  label: "Tables",
  icon: <Table2 size={16} />,
  search: (q) => TABLES.filter((t) => t.label.includes(q)),          // items under @
  toReference: (item) => ({ transport: "object", kind: "table", id: item.id, name: item.label }),
};

<KabooProvider
  runtimeUrl="/api/copilotkit"
  agent={agent}
  references={[uploadProvider({ accept: "image/*,.pdf", onUpload }), tableProvider]}
>
  <CopilotChat input={KabooReferenceInput} messageView={KabooMessageView} />
</KabooProvider>;
```

`KabooReferenceInput` is a drop-in `<CopilotChat input={…}>` slot. It keeps
CopilotKit's native input chrome (send button, disclaimer, theme) but swaps the
plain textarea for a lightweight editor where every reference renders as an
**interactive inline chip**: click a chip to swap it for another, or its `×` to
remove it. The **+** button and the **@** key open the *same* searchable
popover; it dismisses on outside-click / `Escape`. On submit the editor builds
the multimodal message (files as attachment parts, objects on
`state.kaboo_references`, cleared only after the run starts) and runs the agent.
`onUpload` should return a fetchable URL (not base64) so the transport and
persisted event log stay small. See [References & providers](./docs/references.md)
for the full provider contract (both transports, searchable vs action-only,
`toReference`), and kaboo-workflows' *Attachments & Multimodal* chapter for how
references reach each agent.

- [`examples/minimal`](./examples/minimal) — the smallest end-to-end wiring
  (this README's quick start).

## Compatibility & versioning

- **React** 18 and 19 (`react` / `react-dom` >= 18 as peer deps).
- **CopilotKit** `@copilotkit/react-core` >= 1.79.1 (peer dep), the AG-UI 1.0
  generation; kaboo-react 0.10 covers CopilotKit 1.62 to 1.71.1.
- Follows [semantic versioning](https://semver.org). See
  [CHANGELOG.md](./CHANGELOG.md).

## The kaboo stack

kaboo-react is one of three libraries:

- [kaboo-workflows](https://github.com/gl-pgege/kaboo-workflows) — Python
  multi-agent orchestration.
- [kaboo-runtime](https://github.com/gl-pgege/kaboo-runtime) — CopilotKit runtime
  persistence/orchestration plugin.
- **kaboo-react** — this library, the UI layer.

# docs/index.md

# kaboo-react

> React components + hooks for rendering kaboo multi-agent activity in a
> [CopilotKit](https://copilotkit.ai) app, with batteries-included CopilotKit
> integrations.

kaboo-react renders a live, hierarchical view of what your agents are doing —
sub-agent cards, tool calls, streamed tokens, structured outputs, drill-down
navigation, questions and approvals. Sub-agents ride the **same AG-UI run
stream** as the chat, as AG-UI's own `SUBAGENT_*` events, so there is no separate
endpoint to wire up.

## Install

```bash
yarn add @pgege/kaboo-react
# or
npm install @pgege/kaboo-react
# or
pnpm add @pgege/kaboo-react
```

Peer dependencies: `react`, `react-dom`, `@copilotkit/react-core` (>= 1.79.1).

Import the stylesheet once, near your app root:

```ts
import "@pgege/kaboo-react/styles.css";
```

## Quick start

<!-- source: examples/minimal/src/App.tsx#quickstart -->
```tsx
import { CopilotChat } from "@copilotkit/react-core/v2";
import { KabooProvider, GlassTabs, DrillDetailView } from "@pgege/kaboo-react";
import { KabooMessageView } from "@pgege/kaboo-react/copilotkit";
import "@pgege/kaboo-react/styles.css";

export function App({ agent, threadId }: { agent: string; threadId: string }) {
  return (
    <KabooProvider runtimeUrl="/api/copilotkit" agent={agent} threadId={threadId}>
      <GlassTabs />
      <CopilotChat messageView={KabooMessageView} />
      <DrillDetailView />
    </KabooProvider>
  );
}
```

## The kaboo stack

kaboo-react is the UI layer. It pairs with
[kaboo-workflows](https://gl-pgege.github.io/kaboo-workflows/) (agent
orchestration) and [kaboo-runtime](https://gl-pgege.github.io/kaboo-runtime/)
(persistence). See [the kaboo stack](https://gl-pgege.github.io/kaboo-docs/) for
the whole picture.

# docs/getting-started.md

# Getting started

!!! note "Compatibility"
    kaboo-react needs **React 18+**, **Node.js 18+**, and
    **`@copilotkit/react-core` >= 1.79.1** as peers.

This guide wires kaboo-react into a CopilotKit app from scratch.

## Prerequisites

You need a **CopilotKit runtime endpoint** that streams an agent's sub-agents as
AG-UI `SUBAGENT_*` events on the run stream. The
[kaboo-runtime](https://github.com/gl-pgege/kaboo-runtime) package (a CopilotKit
runtime persistence/orchestration plugin) plus a
[kaboo-workflows](https://github.com/gl-pgege/kaboo-workflows) backend is the
canonical server; the
[kaboo-workflows-demo](https://github.com/gl-pgege/kaboo-docs/tree/main/examples/kaboo-workflows-demo)
shows a complete setup.

## Install

```bash
yarn add @pgege/kaboo-react
# or
npm install @pgege/kaboo-react
# or
pnpm add @pgege/kaboo-react
```

Peer dependencies (install if you don't already have them):

```bash
yarn add react react-dom @copilotkit/react-core
```

## Import the stylesheet

Import it once, near your app root:

```ts
import "@pgege/kaboo-react/styles.css";
```

## Wrap your app in `KabooProvider`

`KabooProvider` renders `<CopilotKit>` and nests every kaboo context and handler.
Pass the runtime URL, the entry agent id, and a thread id:

<!-- source: examples/minimal/src/App.tsx#quickstart -->
```tsx
import { CopilotChat } from "@copilotkit/react-core/v2";
import { KabooProvider, GlassTabs, DrillDetailView } from "@pgege/kaboo-react";
import { KabooMessageView } from "@pgege/kaboo-react/copilotkit";
import "@pgege/kaboo-react/styles.css";

export function App({ agent, threadId }: { agent: string; threadId: string }) {
  return (
    <KabooProvider runtimeUrl="/api/copilotkit" agent={agent} threadId={threadId}>
      <GlassTabs />
      <CopilotChat messageView={KabooMessageView} />
      <DrillDetailView />
    </KabooProvider>
  );
}
```

## Render the chat with `KabooMessageView`

Pass `KabooMessageView` to `CopilotChat`'s `messageView` slot. It renders the
normal message list **and** live agent activity cards inside the transcript, from
the moment the first agent starts, and a notice where a run failed. The list
stays CopilotKit's own, so a long thread is virtualized:

```tsx
import { CopilotChat } from "@copilotkit/react-core/v2";
import { KabooMessageView } from "@pgege/kaboo-react/copilotkit";

export function Chat() {
  return <CopilotChat messageView={KabooMessageView} />;
}
```

## Add drill-down

`GlassTabs` renders a breadcrumb once you drill into a sub-agent, and
`DrillDetailView` renders the selected group's detail. Place them alongside the
chat (as in the quick start above).

## What auto-mounts

`KabooProvider` mounts these for you:

- `KabooInlineCards` — inline delegate sub-agent cards at their tool-call
  position.
- `KabooInterruptHandler` — the human-in-the-loop handler.

Escape hatches:

```tsx
import { KabooProvider } from "@pgege/kaboo-react";

export function App({ agent, threadId }: { agent: string; threadId: string }) {
  return (
    <KabooProvider
      runtimeUrl="/api/copilotkit"
      agent={agent}
      threadId={threadId}
      disableInlineCards={false}
      disableInterruptHandler={false}
      copilotKitProps={{}}
    >
      <div />
    </KabooProvider>
  );
}
```

- `disableInlineCards` / `disableInterruptHandler` — skip an auto-mounted handler
  (e.g. to render your own).
- `copilotKitProps` — forward extra props to the underlying `<CopilotKit>`.

## Next steps

- [Concepts](concepts.md) — the data model behind the activity tree.
- [Activity panel & drill-down](activity-panel.md) — render and navigate it.
- [Human-in-the-loop](hitl.md) — approvals, forms, and parallel gates.
- [Troubleshooting](troubleshooting.md) — styles, empty tree, peer versions.

# docs/concepts.md

# Concepts — the data model

How kaboo-react turns an AG-UI stream into the chat, the agent cards and the
canvas you see.

## One stream

Everything rides the **same AG-UI run stream** as the chat — there is no second
endpoint. The entry agent's text and tool calls are the chat. Each agent it
delegates to arrives as AG-UI's own sub-agent events: `SUBAGENT_STARTED`, its
text, reasoning and tool events tagged with its `subagentRunId`, and
`SUBAGENT_FINISHED`. kaboo-react folds those into a tree of `StreamGroup`s that
the chat, the agent cards and the drill-in view all read from. The same fold
runs live and on replay, so a reload draws the same cards.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    Stream["AG-UI run stream"] -->|SUBAGENT_* and tagged events| Fold["kaboo-react fold"]
    Fold --> State["ActivityState<br/>(groups keyed by subagentRunId)"]
    State -->|useActivity| Chat["KabooChat (cards in the transcript)"]
    State -->|useActivity| Panel["drill-in view"]
```

## `StreamGroup` — one sub-agent invocation

Each invocation is a `StreamGroup`, keyed by its `subagentRunId`. The tree is
formed by `parentGroup` (a group id or `null` for a top-level group), and each
top-level group sits in the transcript at the call that started it
(`toolCallId`). The fields you'll touch most:

| Field | Meaning |
|-------|---------|
| `title` / `agentName` | Display title and machine name of the agent. |
| `parentGroup` | Parent group id, or `null` for a top-level group. |
| `toolCallId` | The delegating call the card sits at. |
| `status` | `active` \| `completed` \| `interrupted` \| `error` \| `stopped`. |
| `task` | What this agent was asked to do (shown atop its card). |
| `timeline` | Interleaved text and tool entries, in order. |
| `tools` | Every tool call in the group, in call order, with `toolLabel` when the workflow names it. |
| `structuredOutput` / `outputSchemaName` | Schema-shaped output, and which renderer draws it. |
| `usage` | The agent's token usage. |
| `runIds` | Every run that streamed into the group: a paused agent resumes in a new run. |
| `traceId` | The agent's trace, for feedback scores. |

`ActivityState` also holds `usageByRun` and `traceByRun`, from each run's
`RUN_FINISHED`.

## What the transcript shows

- **A delegate is a card** at the call that started it, not a tool row. Its own
  tool calls render inside it, with the same renderers as the chat.
- **What needs the person is lifted into the transcript.** A delegate's
  question, request or approval shows in the main chat, labelled with the agent,
  while it waits; once answered it stays in the agent's card.
- **Tool calls render as they stream.** Arguments arrive as the model writes
  them, so a renderer can draw a query or a widget before the call runs
  ([Custom tool cards](tool-cards.md)).
- **A failed run says why.** A notice with the run's error follows its last
  message, or the question when the run said nothing, live and on replay.
- **A streaming run re-renders at most every 50 ms** (`throttleMs` on
  `KabooProvider`), and a long thread renders only the rows in view.

## Reading the tree

`useActivity()` returns the groups; helpers navigate them:

```tsx
import { useActivity, topLevelGroups, directChildren } from "@pgege/kaboo-react";

export function RootCount() {
  const { groups } = useActivity();
  const roots = topLevelGroups(groups);
  return <span>{roots.length} root agents</span>;
}
```

See [Activity panel & drill-down](activity-panel.md) for the components that
render this tree, and [Human-in-the-loop](hitl.md) for questions and approvals.

## Shared state and the canvas

The agents' shared state arrives as `STATE_SNAPSHOT` and `STATE_DELTA` events.
Three hooks let a canvas follow the agent:

| Hook | Returns |
|------|---------|
| `useAgentState(select)` | A slice of the shared state, read again whenever the state changes. |
| `useLiveToolCalls(match)` | The calls in flight whose tool name matches, with their arguments so far — for ghost widgets while a plot call streams. |
| `useAgentPresence()` | Which sub-agents are working now, and on which tool. |

```tsx
import { useAgentPresence, useAgentState, useLiveToolCalls } from "@pgege/kaboo-react";

export function CanvasStatus() {
  const dashboards = useAgentState((state) => Object.keys((state.kaboo_workspace as { dashboards?: object })?.dashboards ?? {}));
  const plotting = useLiveToolCalls(/___plot_widgets$/);
  const working = useAgentPresence();
  return (
    <p>
      {dashboards.length} dashboards · {plotting.length} plotting · {working.map((agent) => agent.title).join(", ")}
    </p>
  );
}
```

## Where it sits in the stack

kaboo-react is the UI layer of the
[kaboo stack](https://gl-pgege.github.io/kaboo-docs/):
[kaboo-workflows](https://gl-pgege.github.io/kaboo-workflows/) produces the
stream, [kaboo-runtime](https://gl-pgege.github.io/kaboo-runtime/) persists and
replays it, and kaboo-react renders it.

---

# docs/theming.md

# Theming

kaboo-react ships a single stylesheet and styles everything with CSS variables,
so it blends into your app's design system and is easy to override.

## How styling works

Components read standard design-system tokens with neutral fallbacks:

- `--background`, `--foreground`
- `--card`
- `--muted`, `--muted-foreground`
- `--border`

If your app already defines these (as most design systems / shadcn setups do),
kaboo-react inherits them automatically. Otherwise it falls back to sensible
neutral defaults.

## Import the stylesheet

Import it once, near your app root:

```ts
import "@pgege/kaboo-react/styles.css";
```

The package sets `"sideEffects": ["*.css"]`, so bundlers keep the stylesheet even
with tree-shaking enabled.

## Override tokens

Status colors and other accents are exposed as `--kaboo-*` variables. Set them on
any parent element (e.g. `:root`) to override:

```css
:root {
  --kaboo-running: #d97706;
  --kaboo-warning: #f59e0b;
  --kaboo-success: #16a34a;
}
```

## Dark mode

Because components read `--background` / `--foreground` / `--card` etc., dark mode
works by toggling those tokens the same way you do for the rest of your app (for
example, a `.dark` class on `<html>` that redefines the variables). No
kaboo-specific dark-mode configuration is required.

## Questions and approvals

The question card, the approval card, the batch bar and the permission list use
the same tokens (`--kaboo-card`, `--kaboo-border`, `--kaboo-muted`,
`--kaboo-success`, `--kaboo-success-bg`, `--kaboo-accent`, `--kaboo-warning`)
and a stable set of class names, so you restyle them instead of rebuilding them.
These names are part of the public surface and change only with an entry in the
upgrade guide.

| Element | Class |
|---|---|
| Any request card | `kaboo-interrupt` (with `kaboo-interrupt-approval`, `kaboo-interrupt-form` or `kaboo-interrupt-custom`) |
| Card heading | `kaboo-interrupt-header`, `kaboo-interrupt-message` |
| Buttons | `kaboo-interrupt-btn`, plus `-approve`, `-reject`, `-next`, `-back`, `-skip` |
| Question text, steps | `kaboo-interrupt-question`, `kaboo-interrupt-progress` |
| Options | `kaboo-interrupt-choices`, `kaboo-interrupt-option`, `kaboo-interrupt-option-selected` |
| The Other row | `kaboo-interrupt-option-other`, `kaboo-interrupt-other-input` |
| What a wider approval covers ("Applies to …"), input | `kaboo-approval-covers`, `kaboo-interrupt-details`, `kaboo-interrupt-pre` |
| Approval buttons | `kaboo-approval-actions`, `kaboo-approval-scope` (`-thread`, `-always`), `kaboo-approval-dismiss` |
| Deny with a reason | `kaboo-approval-deny`, `kaboo-approval-reason` |
| Deadline | `kaboo-approval-expiry`, `kaboo-approval-expired` |
| Approve all / Deny all | `kaboo-approval-batch`, `kaboo-approval-batch-count` |
| Answered | `kaboo-interrupt-responded` |
| Remembered permissions | `kaboo-permissions`, `kaboo-permission`, `kaboo-permission-label`, `kaboo-permission-scope`, `kaboo-permission-revoke` |

For example, pill-shaped options and a brand-coloured selection:

```css
.kaboo-interrupt-option {
  border-radius: 999px;
}
.kaboo-interrupt-option-selected,
.kaboo-interrupt-btn-approve {
  border-color: var(--primary);
  background: color-mix(in srgb, var(--primary) 12%, transparent);
  color: var(--primary);
}
```

Replace a card entirely with `interruptRenderers` only when its structure must
change — see [Human-in-the-loop](hitl.md#custom-renderers).

---

# docs/structured-renderers.md

# Structured renderers

Agents can emit **structured output** — a schema-shaped JSON object plus the
schema's name. Structured renderers let you render that object with a custom React
component instead of the default collapsible JSON view.

## What they are

A `StructuredRenderers` map is keyed by the output schema name. Each renderer
receives the structured output object (`Record<string, unknown>`) and returns a
`ReactElement`:

```ts
import { createElement } from "react";
import type { StructuredRenderers } from "@pgege/kaboo-react";

const renderers: StructuredRenderers = {
  WeatherReport: (data) => createElement("div", null, String(data.summary)),
};
```

## Provide renderers

Pass the map to `KabooProvider` (or `KabooActivityProvider` if you compose
providers by hand):

```tsx
import { KabooProvider } from "@pgege/kaboo-react";
import type { StructuredRenderers } from "@pgege/kaboo-react";

const renderers: StructuredRenderers = {
  WeatherReport: (data) => <div>Summary: {String(data.summary)}</div>,
};

export function App({ agent, threadId }: { agent: string; threadId: string }) {
  return (
    <KabooProvider
      runtimeUrl="/api/copilotkit"
      agent={agent}
      threadId={threadId}
      structuredRenderers={renderers}
    >
      <div />
    </KabooProvider>
  );
}
```

## How a renderer is selected

A sub-agent's `SUBAGENT_FINISHED` carries its result and, for a structured
output, the schema's name (`metadata.outputSchema`, kaboo-workflows 0.29 or
later). kaboo-react keeps them on the group as `structuredOutput` (the data) and
`outputSchemaName` (the key), and looks up `renderers[outputSchemaName]`:

- **Match found** → your component renders the data.
- **No match** → a collapsible "Structured output (`<schemaName>`)" view shows
  the data as a readable list.

This means you can add renderers incrementally: unrendered schemas still read
well without one.

To replace how a *tool call* draws rather than how a result object draws, see
[custom tool cards](tool-cards.md).

---

# docs/tool-cards.md

# Custom tool cards

By default every tool call draws as a `ToolRow` — name or label, a summarized
input, a readable result. When a tool means something in your app (a SQL query,
a document it wrote, a ticket it opened), you can replace that row with your own
card: your layout, your click handlers, your drawer.

## Register once

Register a renderer with CopilotKit — `useRenderTool`, or `renderToolCalls` on
`KabooProvider` — and it draws the tool everywhere: in the chat transcript, and
inside every sub-agent's card and drill view, at any depth.

```tsx no-verify
import { useRenderTool } from "@copilotkit/react-core/v2";

declare function openQueryDrawer(toolCallId: string): void;

function RunSqlCard() {
  useRenderTool({
    name: "run_sql",
    render: ({ toolCallId, args, status }) => (
      <button type="button" onClick={() => openQueryDrawer(toolCallId)}>
        <code>{(args as { query?: string }).query ?? "…"}</code>
        {status === "complete" ? "View results" : "Running…"}
      </button>
    ),
  });
  return null;
}
```

Mount it anywhere inside `KabooProvider`. A call that starts a sub-agent is drawn
as that agent's card instead, whatever is registered for its name, so an app
needs no list of its delegate tools.

## Draw it while it streams

Tool arguments arrive as the model writes them — from sub-agents as from the
agent answering the chat — so a card can show the SQL as it's written, or a
widget's outline before it's plotted:

- **`inProgress`** — `args` is partial and grows with each update.
- **`executing`** — the arguments are complete and the tool is running.
- **`complete`** — `result` holds what the tool returned.

Render every status. A card that reads the result unconditionally flashes empty
while the call streams.

## The fallback: `toolRenderers`

`toolRenderers` on `KabooProvider` still draws a tool inside sub-agent timelines
when nothing is registered with CopilotKit for its name. It hands you kaboo's
`ToolCall` — `toolUseId`, `toolName`, `toolLabel`, `toolInput`, `toolResult`,
`status` — rather than CopilotKit's render props:

```tsx
import { KabooProvider } from "@pgege/kaboo-react";
import type { ToolRenderers, ToolRendererProps } from "@pgege/kaboo-react";

declare function openQueryDrawer(toolCallId: string): void;

function RunSqlRow({ tool }: ToolRendererProps) {
  const input = tool.toolInput as { query?: string } | undefined;
  return (
    <button type="button" disabled={tool.status === "running"} onClick={() => openQueryDrawer(tool.toolUseId)}>
      <code>{input?.query ?? "…"}</code>
    </button>
  );
}

const toolRenderers: ToolRenderers = { run_sql: RunSqlRow };

export function App({ agent, threadId }: { agent: string; threadId: string }) {
  return (
    <KabooProvider runtimeUrl="/api/copilotkit" agent={agent} threadId={threadId} toolRenderers={toolRenderers}>
      <div />
    </KabooProvider>
  );
}
```

An approval on a gated tool still renders with your card, so a custom renderer
never hides a pending question.

## Status, errors and timing

Inside an agent's timeline, every renderer (CopilotKit's, `toolRenderers` and
the fallback) can read its call's state with `useToolCallMeta()`: `status`
(`running`, `success`, `error` or `cancelled`), the `label` the agent gave it,
`error` and `fix` when it failed, `startedAt` and `endedAt`, `toolCallId` and
`agentName`. It returns `null` outside a timeline.

```tsx
import { useToolCallMeta } from "@pgege/kaboo-react";

export function CallStatus() {
  const meta = useToolCallMeta();
  if (!meta) return null;
  if (meta.status === "error") return <p role="alert">{meta.error}{meta.fix ? ` ${meta.fix}` : ""}</p>;
  const took = meta.startedAt !== undefined && meta.endedAt !== undefined ? meta.endedAt - meta.startedAt : undefined;
  return <span>{meta.label ?? meta.status}{took !== undefined ? ` · ${took} ms` : ""}</span>;
}
```

A registered renderer gets a failed or cancelled call with CopilotKit's
`complete` status, so it stops spinning; this hook says which it was.

A call the chat's own agent made, outside any timeline, reads its outcome with
`useToolOutcome(toolCallId)`: `status` (`success` or `error`), and `error` and
`fix` when it failed, as kaboo-workflows 0.34 reports them on every result. It
is `undefined` while the call runs and for results from older services, which
carry no status; never guess a failure from the result's text.

```tsx
import { useRenderTool } from "@copilotkit/react-core/v2";
import { useToolOutcome } from "@pgege/kaboo-react";

const anyArguments = {
  "~standard": { version: 1 as const, vendor: "app", validate: (value: unknown) => ({ value }) },
};

function Outcome({ toolCallId }: { toolCallId: string }) {
  const outcome = useToolOutcome(toolCallId);
  return outcome?.status === "error" ? <p role="alert">{outcome.error}</p> : null;
}

export function RunSqlOutcome() {
  useRenderTool({
    name: "run_sql",
    parameters: anyArguments,
    render: ({ toolCallId }) => <Outcome toolCallId={toolCallId} />,
  });
  return null;
}
```

The fallback renderer gets the same outcome on the `ToolCall` it is handed:
`status`, `error` and `fix`.

## Every other tool: `fallbackToolRenderer`

`fallbackToolRenderer` replaces the built-in `ToolRow` for any tool with no
renderer of its own, in agent timelines and in the chat, so an app can give
every call the same frame. `isReadOnlyTool` tells the timeline which tools only
read, and folds two or more consecutive reads into one row ("Read 3 items")
that expands to the calls:

```tsx
import { KabooProvider, useToolCallMeta } from "@pgege/kaboo-react";
import type { ToolRendererProps } from "@pgege/kaboo-react";

function AnyTool({ tool }: ToolRendererProps) {
  const meta = useToolCallMeta();
  return (
    <div>
      {tool.toolLabel ?? tool.toolName} · {meta?.status ?? tool.status}
    </div>
  );
}

const READS = /___(get|list|read|search)_/;

export function App({ agent, threadId }: { agent: string; threadId: string }) {
  return (
    <KabooProvider
      runtimeUrl="/api/copilotkit"
      agent={agent}
      threadId={threadId}
      fallbackToolRenderer={AnyTool}
      isReadOnlyTool={(name) => READS.test(name)}
    >
      <div />
    </KabooProvider>
  );
}
```

## Making a card interactive

The card is ordinary React inside your app's tree, so a click handler may open a
drawer, route, or mutate — nothing has to travel through the agent. Two things
are worth getting right:

- **Key by the call's id, not by tool name or index.** A tool can be called many
  times in one run, and a timeline re-renders as the run streams.
- **Fetch by reference.** If the card needs data the tool call doesn't carry,
  fetch it in the card from your own API by the ids in the arguments rather than
  widening the tool's result — the result is transcript, and it is replayed on
  every reconnect.

## Choosing between a tool card and structured output

A tool card is right when the *call* is the thing worth showing. When the agent
is producing a result object with a schema — a report, a risk matrix, a table —
use a [structured renderer](structured-renderers.md) instead, keyed by the
schema name rather than the tool name.

Lab scenarios:
[plain-dashboard](https://github.com/gl-pgege/kaboo-docs/blob/main/examples/kaboo-workflows-demo/scenarios/plain-dashboard.yaml)
and
[delegate-dashboard](https://github.com/gl-pgege/kaboo-docs/blob/main/examples/kaboo-workflows-demo/scenarios/delegate-dashboard.yaml).

---

# docs/references.md

# References & providers

Let users **attach things to a message** — files *and* your own domain entities
(tables, dashboards, tickets, customers, …). Everything is driven by
**reference providers** you register on `<KabooProvider references={…}>` and the
`KabooReferenceInput` composer slot.

This guide covers what a provider is, the two transports, and how to write your
own. The backend half — making a reference actually reach an agent — is covered
in kaboo-workflows' *Attachments & Multimodal* chapter.

## Mental model

A **provider** is a pluggable source of "things you can reference" in the shared
`+` / `@` popover. It answers three questions:

1. **What can be referenced?** — the items it lists (`search`) or the action it
   runs (`onSelect`, e.g. a file picker).
2. **How is it shown in the picker?** — its `label`, `icon`, and optional
   `renderItem`.
3. **What does a chosen one become on the wire?** — `toReference`, which maps a
   selection to a `PendingReference` with a *transport*.

When the user picks an item, the composer stages it as a chip and, on submit,
serializes it onto the outgoing message according to its transport.

!!! note "Providers don't style chips"
    A provider controls how an item looks **in the popover menu** (`icon`,
    `renderItem`) and what it *becomes* (`toReference`). It does **not** control
    how the chip renders in the editor or the sent bubble — that is centralized
    in `KabooReferenceInput` / `KabooUserMessage` and derived from the
    reference's transport, mime type, and name.

## The two transports

Every reference reaches the agent as one of two transports:

| Transport    | For                                   | Carries bytes? | Serialized as                                   | Resolved by                                  |
| ------------ | ------------------------------------- | -------------- | ----------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------- |
| `attachment` | files/blobs (pdf, image, csv, …)      | yes            | a CopilotKit `InputContent` part on the message | the built-in `fetch_attachment` tool         |
| `object`     | pointers to *your* entities           | no             | an entry in `state.kaboo_references`            | *your* MCP tool (per `kind`)                 |

`attachment` is the only blob-capable transport. An `object` is just a pointer
`{ kind, id, name }`; your backend resolves it on demand.

## Register providers

Pass providers to `KabooProvider` and use the `KabooReferenceInput` slot:

```tsx no-verify
import { CopilotChat } from "@copilotkit/react-core/v2";
import {
  KabooProvider,
  KabooReferenceInput,
  uploadProvider,
} from "@pgege/kaboo-react";
import { KabooMessageView } from "@pgege/kaboo-react/copilotkit";
import { tableProvider } from "./references";

<KabooProvider
  runtimeUrl="/api/copilotkit"
  agent={agent}
  threadId={threadId}
  references={[uploadProvider({ accept: "image/*,.pdf", onUpload }), tableProvider]}
>
  <CopilotChat input={KabooReferenceInput} messageView={KabooMessageView} />
</KabooProvider>;
```

## Anatomy of a `ReferenceProvider`

```ts no-verify
interface ReferenceProvider<T = unknown> {
  id: string;                                          // stable provider id
  label: string;                                       // group heading in the menu
  icon?: ReactNode;                                    // icon beside the heading
  search?: (query: string) =>                          // omit → action-only
    ReferenceItem<T>[] | Promise<ReferenceItem<T>[]>;
  renderItem?: (item: ReferenceItem<T>) => ReactNode;  // custom menu row
  onSelect?: (item: ReferenceItem<T>) => void | Promise<void>; // side effect on choose
  toReference?: (item: ReferenceItem<T>) => PendingReference;   // becomes this on the wire
}

// Each searchable item; `data` is provider-defined and threaded to toReference.
interface ReferenceItem<T = unknown> {
  id: string;
  label: string;         // default chip text
  description?: string;  // optional secondary line
  data?: T;
}
```

A provider is either:

- **searchable** — supplies `search`, so its items list live in the menu as the
  user types; or
- **action-only** — omits `search`; selecting its group row runs `onSelect`
  (e.g. opening a file dialog). The built-in `uploadProvider` is action-only.

## Write an object provider

Three fields make a custom entity referenceable — `search` (what to list),
`toReference` (what it becomes), and `icon` (how it's grouped):

```tsx
import { Table2 } from "lucide-react";
import type { ReferenceProvider } from "@pgege/kaboo-react";

const TABLES = [
  { id: "companies", label: "companies", description: "Vendors and company profiles" },
  { id: "products", label: "products", description: "Product catalog with pricing" },
];

export const tableProvider: ReferenceProvider = {
  id: "table",
  label: "Tables",
  icon: <Table2 size={16} />,
  // Items listed under @ for the current query.
  search: (q) =>
    TABLES.filter((t) => t.label.toLowerCase().includes(q.toLowerCase())),
  // How a chosen item serializes onto the message.
  toReference: (item) => ({
    transport: "object",
    kind: "table",
    id: item.id,
    name: item.label,
    meta: { description: item.description },
  }),
};
```

The selected object syncs into `state.kaboo_references` and appears inline as an
`@name` chip. Your backend resolves the `{ kind: "table", id }` pointer with its
own tool. Add more object kinds (dashboards, tickets, …) by registering more
providers with distinct `kind`s.

!!! tip "`meta` rides along"
    Anything you put in `toReference(...).meta` travels in `state.kaboo_references`
    and is available to your resolver tool — handy for extra context the id
    alone doesn't capture.

`search` may be async and is called on every keystroke. Every provider is
searched at once, a search that rejects drops that provider's rows rather than
the menu, and an answer that arrives after the user has typed further is
discarded — so a slow provider costs latency, never wrong rows. Debouncing or
caching on your side is still worth it if the query hits a network.

## Files: the built-in `uploadProvider`

File upload ships as a provider. Register it with your `onUpload`:

```tsx
import { uploadProvider } from "@pgege/kaboo-react";
import type { AttachmentUploadResult } from "@copilotkit/shared";

async function onUpload(file: File): Promise<AttachmentUploadResult> {
  const form = new FormData();
  form.append("file", file);
  const res = await fetch("/api/upload", { method: "POST", body: form });
  const { url, mimeType } = await res.json();
  return { type: "url", value: url, mimeType }; // a fetchable URL
}

uploadProvider({ accept: "image/*,.pdf,.csv,.txt,.md", maxSize: 20 * 1024 * 1024, onUpload });
```

- **Return a URL, not base64.** The server fetches attachment URLs with no auth
  (presigned/public pattern), which keeps the AG-UI transport *and* the
  persisted event log small.
- **`onUpload` is optional.** Omit it and the file is inlined as base64 — fine
  for small files/tests, but it bloats storage for large ones.
- `accept` and `maxSize` gate the picker; oversized files are rejected before
  upload.

Choosing "Attach a file" (from **+** or **@**) opens the picker, uploads, and
drops a file chip. The file rides the message as an `InputContent` part stamped
with `kaboo_id` / `kaboo_kind` / `kaboo_name` metadata.

## Action-only providers

Omit `search` to make the group row itself an action. Use `onSelect` for the
side effect; produce the reference either synchronously via `toReference` or
asynchronously (as `uploadProvider` does through its upload callback):

```tsx no-verify
const pickFromDrive: ReferenceProvider = {
  id: "drive",
  label: "Google Drive",
  icon: <DriveIcon />,
  onSelect: async () => {
    /* open your picker, upload, and stage the reference */
  },
};
```

## What a chosen item becomes

`toReference` returns a `PendingReference`:

```ts
type PendingReference =
  | { transport: "attachment"; kind: string; id: string; name: string;
      mimeType: string; source: { url: string } | { data: string } }
  | { transport: "object"; kind: string; id: string; name: string;
      meta?: Record<string, unknown> };
```

On submit the composer:

- appends each **attachment** as a message content part (with the `kaboo_*`
  metadata), and
- writes each **object** into `state.kaboo_references`.

The `id` you mint is the same id the backend lists in its manifest and passes to
a resolver tool, so both stacks agree without translation.

## What providers do *not* do

- They don't render the selected chip (editor or bubble) — that's centralized.
- They don't decide the per-agent policy (`reference` / `inline` / tool
  availability) — that's the backend's `attachments:` config.

## Next steps

- [Getting started](getting-started.md) — wire kaboo-react into a CopilotKit app.
- [Theming](theming.md) — restyle chips and the composer via CSS variables.
- kaboo-workflows *Attachments & Multimodal* — how references reach each agent
  (manifest, `fetch_attachment`, inline media).

---

# docs/hitl.md

# Human-in-the-loop

When an agent needs the person, kaboo-react shows the request in the chat and
the agent carries on with the answer. There are two mechanisms:

- **Questions and requests** are tools the browser runs. `useAskUserTool`
  registers `ask_user`; `useRequestTool` registers any other request (a file,
  a data source) with your own panel. An agent calls them only when its
  workflow allows it (kaboo-workflows' `client_tools`), delegates included.
- **Approvals** pause the run on an interrupt, and the built-in
  `KabooInterruptHandler` draws the card on CopilotKit's `useInterrupt`. Apps
  add their own interrupt kinds with their own renderers.

A request waits with no time limit. The pause lives in the stored conversation,
so the person can close the tab, come back days later on another device, and
answer; if they send a message instead, the request is skipped.

## Questions

```tsx
import { useAskUserTool } from "@pgege/kaboo-react";
import { KabooChat } from "@pgege/kaboo-react/copilotkit";

export function Chat() {
  useAskUserTool();
  return <KabooChat />;
}
```

Questions are multiple choice, like Cursor's:

- Each question offers the agent's options, single or multi-select.
- Every question has an **Other** row with its own text field, so the person
  can always answer in their own words.
- **Submit** sends the answers once every question has one; **Skip** answers
  nothing. Several questions step through with Next and Back.

The answer is a `{question: answer}` map — a string, a list for multi-select,
the person's own words for Other — and the answered Q&A stays in the
transcript. A call whose arguments don't match the tool's schema is answered
with an error naming the problem, so the model asks again properly instead of
the person seeing a broken card.

## Requests

```tsx
import { toolSchema, useRequestTool, type KabooRequestRenderProps } from "@pgege/kaboo-react";

interface DatasourcesArgs {
  reason: string;
  kinds: string[];
}

const requestDatasources = toolSchema<DatasourcesArgs>(
  {
    type: "object",
    properties: { reason: { type: "string" }, kinds: { type: "array", items: { type: "string" } } },
    required: ["reason", "kinds"],
  },
  (value) => (Array.isArray((value as { kinds?: unknown })?.kinds) ? [] : ["kinds must be a list"]),
);

function DatasourcesPanel({ args, status, answer, skip }: KabooRequestRenderProps<DatasourcesArgs>) {
  if (status !== "waiting") return null;
  return (
    <div className="kaboo-interrupt">
      <p>{args.reason}</p>
      <button onClick={() => answer({ datasources: args.kinds })}>Use all</button>
      <button onClick={skip}>Skip</button>
    </div>
  );
}

export function BrowserTools() {
  useRequestTool({
    name: "request_datasources",
    description: "Ask the person to pick data sources and wait for the choice.",
    parameters: requestDatasources,
    render: DatasourcesPanel,
  });
  return null;
}
```

`parameters` takes any Standard Schema, such as a zod schema, or one built with
`toolSchema`. The panel gets the call's `args`, its `status`, and `answer` and
`skip`. An object passed to `answer` is sent as JSON; `skip` tells the agent the
person declined. Define the panel outside the component that registers it, so it
keeps its state.

## Several requests at once

One agent's questions show as one card that steps through them. When several
agents wait — parallel delegates asking at once — their requests show one at a
time, in the order they were asked, and the next waits under "Up next" until the
one above is answered. A delegate's request shows in the main transcript,
labelled with the agent, while it waits; once answered, the Q&A stays in that
agent's card.

## Approvals

The approval card shows what the agent wants to run (with its input under "View
input") and the options the request offers:

- **Approve** runs the call once.
- **Allow for this chat** and **Always allow** appear when the agent offers
  them — which it does only when the host remembers decisions (kaboo-runtime
  with a grant store), or when a tool that enforces its own approvals offers
  them. Above the buttons, "Applies to …" names what they cover (the request's
  `subject.label`, such as "catalog changes in Summit Outfitters"). Either
  also approves the other waiting requests with the same subject.
- **Deny** asks for an optional reason the agent will read.
- With a deadline, the card shows how long it stays answerable; once it has
  passed, only **Dismiss** remains.

With two or more approvals waiting, **Approve all** and **Deny all** appear.
A delegate's approval shows at its real tool row, labelled with the agent.

A tool that enforces its own approvals (kaboo-workflows'
`interrupt.tool_approvals`) raises the same approval request, so the same card
renders it. Its `reason.request` is the tool's own request ID; the card sends
the same answers, and the host forwards the decision to the tool's service.

## What each answer sends

| The person… | `onResolve` / `onCancel` | The agent |
|---|---|---|
| approves | `onResolve({ status: "approved", scope })` | runs the call |
| denies | `onResolve({ status: "cancelled", reason? })` | cancels it and reads the reason |
| skips or dismisses | `onCancel()` | cancels it as skipped |

A denial is sent as `cancelled` so an agent that predates denial reasons can
never mistake it for an approval.

The answers resume the turn in a new run, and the chat still shows one turn:
the `turnFooter` slot renders after the turn's last reply, and its `runIds`
list every run the turn spanned, so anything your app keys by run (files or
versions the turn made) is found under one of them.

## Moving on

If the person sends a message while a question, request or approval waits, what
was waiting is skipped and the agent answers the message. You do not need to
block the composer: sending through `KabooChat` or `useKabooSend` answers each
open request with "Skipped: the person sent a message instead of answering" and
cancels each open approval in the same run as the new message.

## When an answer can't be recorded

Sometimes answers never reach the agent: the host refuses a decision (its
approval service is down, or doesn't take it), or the request itself fails. The
requests are still open on the server, so the built-in handler brings them back
to be answered again, with the reason above them. Pass `onInterruptError` to
show the reason somewhere else too, such as a toast:

```tsx
import { CopilotChat } from "@copilotkit/react-core/v2";
import { KabooProvider } from "@pgege/kaboo-react";

declare function showToast(message: string): void;

export function Chat({ threadId }: { threadId: string }) {
  return (
    <KabooProvider runtimeUrl="/api/copilotkit" agent="assistant" threadId={threadId} onInterruptError={showToast}>
      <CopilotChat />
    </KabooProvider>
  );
}
```

The reason is the message of the run's `RUN_ERROR`, which kaboo-runtime takes
from the error the host's `onDecision` throws, so the host should throw one a
person can act on. A run that fails after the agent started working is left to
the chat's usual error handling.

## Choosing the approval options

`approvalScopes` on `KabooProvider` narrows what the approval card offers for
the whole app. A request offers only the scopes both the agent and the app
allow; Approve (`once`) is always offered.

```tsx
import { KabooProvider } from "@pgege/kaboo-react";

export function App({ agent, threadId }: { agent: string; threadId: string }) {
  return (
    <KabooProvider
      runtimeUrl="/api/copilotkit"
      agent={agent}
      threadId={threadId}
      approvalScopes={["once", "thread"]}
    >
      <div />
    </KabooProvider>
  );
}
```

## Styling

The built-in cards read the theme tokens and use a stable set of class names, so
most apps restyle them rather than replace them — see
[Theming](theming.md#questions-and-approvals).

## Custom cards

### A custom approval card that keeps the standard options

`interruptRenderers` replaces the UI for an interrupt kind: the built-in
`approval`, or an app's own kind. Render your own summary and reuse
`ApprovalActions` (or `useApprovalDecision` for your own buttons), so the
scopes, deny reason, deadline and batch behaviour stay standard:

```tsx
import { ApprovalActions, KabooProvider } from "@pgege/kaboo-react";
import type { ApprovalReason, InterruptRendererProps } from "@pgege/kaboo-react";

function ChangeCard(props: InterruptRendererProps<ApprovalReason>) {
  return (
    <div className="kaboo-interrupt">
      <p>{props.reason.subject?.label ?? props.reason.tool_name}</p>
      <ApprovalActions {...props} />
    </div>
  );
}

export function App({ agent, threadId }: { agent: string; threadId: string }) {
  return (
    <KabooProvider
      runtimeUrl="/api/copilotkit"
      agent={agent}
      threadId={threadId}
      interruptRenderers={{ approval: ChangeCard }}
    >
      <div />
    </KabooProvider>
  );
}
```

### A custom question card

Pass `render` to `useAskUserTool`. Read questions with `toFormQuestion` and
answer with `buildAnswerPayload`, so the agent and the answered Q&A card
receive the same answer as from the built-in card:

```tsx
import { useState } from "react";
import { buildAnswerPayload, toFormQuestion, useAskUserTool } from "@pgege/kaboo-react";
import type { AskUserArgs, KabooRequestRenderProps } from "@pgege/kaboo-react";

function ChipQuestions({ args, status, answer, skip }: KabooRequestRenderProps<AskUserArgs>) {
  const questions = args.questions.map(toFormQuestion);
  const [answers, setAnswers] = useState<Record<number, string>>({});
  if (status !== "waiting") return null;
  return (
    <div>
      {questions.map((q, idx) => (
        <fieldset key={q.question}>
          <legend>{q.question}</legend>
          {q.options.map((option) => (
            <button key={option} onClick={() => setAnswers({ ...answers, [idx]: option })}>
              {option}
            </button>
          ))}
        </fieldset>
      ))}
      <button onClick={() => answer(buildAnswerPayload(questions, answers))}>Send</button>
      <button onClick={skip}>Skip</button>
    </div>
  );
}

export function Questions() {
  useAskUserTool({ render: ChipQuestions });
  return null;
}
```

### An app's own interrupt kind

A server tool that needs something only the server can check raises its own
interrupt kind (`type: "account"`), and the app registers a renderer for it.
Its fields arrive on `reason`. A kind with no registered renderer gets a minimal
card with its `message` and Skip, so the chat never stalls. Prefer a browser
request (`useRequestTool`) when the server needs nothing but the answer.

```tsx
import { KabooProvider } from "@pgege/kaboo-react";
import type { InterruptRendererProps } from "@pgege/kaboo-react";

interface AccountRequest {
  type: string;
  message?: string;
  accounts?: string[];
}

function AccountPicker({ reason, onResolve, onCancel }: InterruptRendererProps<AccountRequest>) {
  return (
    <div>
      <p>{reason.message}</p>
      {(reason.accounts ?? []).map((account) => (
        <button key={account} onClick={() => onResolve({ account })}>
          {account}
        </button>
      ))}
      <button onClick={onCancel}>Skip</button>
    </div>
  );
}

export function App({ agent, threadId }: { agent: string; threadId: string }) {
  return (
    <KabooProvider
      runtimeUrl="/api/copilotkit"
      agent={agent}
      threadId={threadId}
      interruptRenderers={{ account: AccountPicker }}
    >
      <div />
    </KabooProvider>
  );
}
```

## Remembered permissions

When the person chooses "Always allow", the host remembers it (kaboo-runtime's
`runner.listGrants` / `revokeGrant`). `PermissionList` renders the list with a
Revoke button each; your app loads and revokes through its own API:

```tsx
import { PermissionList, type RememberedPermission } from "@pgege/kaboo-react";

export function AssistantPermissions({
  grants,
  revoke,
}: {
  grants: RememberedPermission[];
  revoke: (id: string) => void;
}) {
  return <PermissionList grants={grants} onRevoke={revoke} />;
}
```

Lab scenarios:
[question-several](https://github.com/gl-pgege/kaboo-docs/blob/main/examples/kaboo-workflows-demo/scenarios/question-several.yaml),
[question-parallel](https://github.com/gl-pgege/kaboo-docs/blob/main/examples/kaboo-workflows-demo/scenarios/question-parallel.yaml),
[request-datasources](https://github.com/gl-pgege/kaboo-docs/blob/main/examples/kaboo-workflows-demo/scenarios/request-datasources.yaml),
[approval-subagent](https://github.com/gl-pgege/kaboo-docs/blob/main/examples/kaboo-workflows-demo/scenarios/approval-subagent.yaml)
and
[approval-grant](https://github.com/gl-pgege/kaboo-docs/blob/main/examples/kaboo-workflows-demo/scenarios/approval-grant.yaml).

---

# docs/activity-panel.md

# Activity panel & drill-down

kaboo-react models agent work as a **tree of groups** and gives you components to
render and navigate it.

## The activity tree

Activity is a set of `StreamGroup`s keyed by group id, exposed by `useActivity()`.
Each group links to its parent via `parentGroup`, forming the hierarchy. Read the
root groups with `topLevelGroups`:

```tsx
import { useActivity, topLevelGroups } from "@pgege/kaboo-react";

export function RootAgents() {
  const { groups } = useActivity();
  return <div>{topLevelGroups(groups).length} root agents</div>;
}
```

## Rendering primitives

- **`ActivityPanel`** — renders the current level of the tree as a list of
  `AgentCard`s. Use it for a standalone activity view (outside the chat).
- **`AgentCard`** — one agent run: title, status, task, timeline, result.
- **`Timeline`** — the chronological text/tool stream inside a card.
- **`ToolRow`** — a single tool call (input summary + result).
- **`MiniTable`** — tabular tool results.

```tsx
import { ActivityPanel } from "@pgege/kaboo-react";

export function Sidebar() {
  return (
    <aside>
      <ActivityPanel />
    </aside>
  );
}
```

## Drill-down

To let users explore sub-agents, pair the breadcrumb and detail components:

```tsx
import { GlassTabs, DrillDetailView } from "@pgege/kaboo-react";

export function DrillArea() {
  return (
    <>
      <GlassTabs />
      <DrillDetailView />
    </>
  );
}
```

- **`GlassTabs`** — breadcrumb of the drill path (renders nothing at the root).
- **`DrillDetailView`** — the drilled-in group's full detail.
- **`useDrill()`** — the navigation state and actions (`drillIn`, `drillUp`,
  `drillToRoot`, `drillToLevel`).

```tsx
import { useDrill } from "@pgege/kaboo-react";

export function BackButton() {
  const { drillUp, activeDrill } = useDrill();
  if (!activeDrill) return null;
  return <button onClick={drillUp}>Back</button>;
}
```

## Group helpers

- **`topLevelGroups(groups)`** — the parentless roots.
- **`directChildren(groups, parentId)`** — one level of children.

```ts
import { directChildren } from "@pgege/kaboo-react";

export function childCount(
  groups: Parameters<typeof directChildren>[0],
  parentId: string,
) {
  return directChildren(groups, parentId).length;
}
```

---

# docs/copilotkit-subpath.md

# The `@pgege/kaboo-react/copilotkit` subpath

kaboo-react ships two barrels:

- **`kaboo-react`** — framework-agnostic contexts, hooks, components, and utils.
- **`@pgege/kaboo-react/copilotkit`** — integrations coupled to CopilotKit's chat
  surfaces.

## Why a separate barrel

The `copilotkit` integrations plug into specific slots of `CopilotChat` and depend
on CopilotKit's v2 APIs. Keeping them behind a subpath makes that coupling
explicit and keeps the main barrel usable in more contexts.

## The exports

| Export | Purpose | Wiring |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `KabooChat` | `CopilotChat` with kaboo's transcript and the sub-agent drill-down; its composer sends through `useKabooSend`, so a new message skips open requests. | Render it in place of `CopilotChat`. |
| `KabooMessageView` | Live in-chat member cards, and what needs the person lifted into the transcript. | `CopilotChat` `messageView` slot. |
| `KabooAssistantMessage` | Cards above a settled assistant reply. | Used by `KabooMessageView` (assistant-message slot). |
| `KabooInlineCards` | Delegate sub-agent cards at the tool-call position. | Auto-mounted by `KabooProvider`. |
| `KabooInterruptHandler` | Approvals and an app's own interrupt kinds, on `useInterrupt`. | Auto-mounted by `KabooProvider`. |
| `KabooToolRender` | Wildcard tool renderer. | Used by `KabooInlineCards`. |
| `withSubagentLabel` | Wraps an activity renderer (an A2UI surface) so a sub-agent's surface is labelled with the agent. | Pass to `renderActivityMessages`. |

Most apps only render **`KabooChat`** — the rest are auto-mounted by
`KabooProvider`.

## Wiring `KabooMessageView`

```tsx
import { CopilotChat } from "@copilotkit/react-core/v2";
import { KabooMessageView } from "@pgege/kaboo-react/copilotkit";

export function Chat() {
  return <CopilotChat messageView={KabooMessageView} />;
}
```

`KabooMessageView` is a drop-in `messageView`: it carries a `Cursor` static like
CopilotKit's own message view, so it satisfies the slot type directly.

## Using the handlers yourself

If you disable an auto-mounted handler on `KabooProvider`
(`disableInterruptHandler` / `disableInlineCards`), you can mount your own from
this subpath:

```tsx
import { KabooProvider } from "@pgege/kaboo-react";
import { KabooInterruptHandler } from "@pgege/kaboo-react/copilotkit";

export function App({ agent, threadId }: { agent: string; threadId: string }) {
  return (
    <KabooProvider
      runtimeUrl="/api/copilotkit"
      agent={agent}
      threadId={threadId}
      disableInterruptHandler
    >
      <KabooInterruptHandler agentId={agent} />
    </KabooProvider>
  );
}
```

---

# docs/troubleshooting.md

# Troubleshooting

## Components render unstyled

Import the stylesheet **once**, near your app root:

```ts
import "@pgege/kaboo-react/styles.css";
```

Without it, cards, tabs, and the activity panel have no layout or theme. See
[Theming](theming.md) to customize the `--kaboo-*` tokens.

## The activity tree is empty

Groups come from `SUBAGENT_*` events on the AG-UI run stream. If
`useActivity()` returns no groups:

- Confirm the agent delegates — a plain agent with no sub-agents has no groups;
  its work is the chat itself.
- Confirm the backend emits sub-agent events — an agent served by
  [kaboo-workflows](https://gl-pgege.github.io/kaboo-workflows/) 0.29 or later
  does.
- Confirm `KabooProvider`'s `runtimeUrl` points at that backend and the request
  isn't blocked (check the network tab / dev-proxy). The
  [minimal example](https://github.com/gl-pgege/kaboo-react/tree/main/examples/minimal)
  proxies `/api` to `http://localhost:4000`.

## Approval cards stay "Response submitted"

The answers were sent but never reached the agent: the host refused a decision,
or the run failed before the agent started. Before 0.11.2 the cards stayed
answered until a reload. From 0.11.2 they come back to be answered again, with
the reason above them (see
[When an answer can't be recorded](hitl.md#when-an-answer-cant-be-recorded)).
Pair it with kaboo-runtime 0.7.1 or later, which opens such runs with
`RUN_STARTED`. Then fix the refusal itself on the host.

## Peer / version errors

kaboo-react needs `react`, `react-dom`, and `@copilotkit/react-core` (**>= 1.79.1**)
as peers. Install/upgrade them if you see missing-module or hook-mismatch
errors:

```bash
yarn add react react-dom @copilotkit/react-core
```

A CopilotKit version below 1.79.1 can cause `KabooProvider` / `CopilotChat`
mismatches — align to a supported version, or stay on kaboo-react 0.10 for
CopilotKit 1.62 to 1.71.1.

## `KabooMessageView` import fails

`KabooMessageView` lives in the CopilotKit subpath barrel:

```ts
import { KabooMessageView } from "@pgege/kaboo-react/copilotkit";
```

See [CopilotKit subpath](copilotkit-subpath.md) for what that barrel exports and
why it's separate from the root entry.

---

# docs/upgrading.md

# Upgrading

What changes between releases that you might have to act on, with the code
before and after. If none of a release's items apply to you, upgrading is a
version bump.

The kaboo libraries can be upgraded in any order: this release reads what older
agents send, and nothing it sends can be mistaken for an approval by an older
agent. Features that span the stack light up once every piece is upgraded — see
[Upgrading the stack](https://gl-pgege.github.io/kaboo-docs/start-here/#upgrading-the-stack).

## 0.14

0.14 reads the status kaboo-workflows 0.34 puts on every tool result and the
`kaboo.run_error` event kaboo-runtime replays where a run failed; with older
services, top-level calls carry no outcome and only live failures show.

### Delegate tools need no renderer of their own

**Who:** apps that map their delegate tools to a card that draws the
sub-agent's `AgentCard`.

A call that started a sub-agent now draws that agent's card inside a timeline
by itself. Drop the mapping:

```diff
- const toolRenderers: ToolRenderers = { analyze_sql: DelegateCard, sql_visualizer: DelegateCard };
- <KabooProvider toolRenderers={toolRenderers} … />
+ <KabooProvider … />
```

### Top-level failures come from the result, not its text

**Who:** apps that decide a top-level call failed by reading its result.

Read `useToolOutcome(toolCallId)` instead; the fallback renderer gets the same
`status`, `error` and `fix` on its `ToolCall`. See
[Custom tool cards](tool-cards.md#status-errors-and-timing).

### Re-renders are throttled, and the message list is CopilotKit's own

**Who:** apps that wrap `KabooMessageView` or count on a render per event.

A streaming run re-renders at most every 50 ms; pass `throttleMs={0}` to
`KabooProvider` for one per event. `KabooMessageView` hands CopilotKit's list
no children render prop, so a long thread is virtualized; the cards waiting for
a reply and the run-start indicator render after the list, and CopilotKit's own
cursor is hidden. A failed run adds a `kaboo-run-error` activity message to the
list, so a `groupMessages` that handles activity messages sees it.

## 0.13.1

**Who:** no one needs to change anything.

An agent card that mounts already finished, such as on a replayed thread,
starts collapsed, as a card that finishes while you watch already did. Click
its header to open it.

## 0.13

0.13 reads what kaboo-workflows 0.32 adds to tool results (an error status, the
error and its fix, a label, and JSON previews that record what they cut), and
still reads older agents: their calls simply never fail. It needs no
CopilotKit change.

### Registered renderers get failed and cancelled calls as complete

**Who:** apps that register tool renderers with CopilotKit (`useRenderTool`,
`renderToolCalls`).

A call that failed, or that its run abandoned, used to stay `executing`, so the
card spun forever. It now reaches your renderer as `complete`, and
`useToolCallMeta()` says what really happened:

```diff
  render: ({ status, result }) =>
-   status === "complete" ? <Done result={result} /> : <Spinner />
+   status === "complete" ? <Finished result={result} /> : <Spinner />

+ function Finished({ result }: { result?: string }) {
+   const meta = useToolCallMeta();
+   if (meta?.status === "error") return <Failed message={meta.error} fix={meta.fix} />;
+   if (meta?.status === "cancelled") return <Stopped />;
+   return <Done result={result} />;
+ }
```

`useToolCallMeta()` returns `null` outside an agent's timeline. See
[Custom tool cards](tool-cards.md#status-errors-and-timing).

### Tool rows and status dots

**Who:** apps that restyle `.kaboo-tool-dot-*`.

The row is one line (icon, label, target, status icon and duration) and a
finished call shows a check instead of the word "done". The status icons are
drawn with `currentColor`, so their classes set `color`:

```diff
- .kaboo-tool-dot-success { fill: green; }
+ .kaboo-tool-dot-success { color: green; }
```

A failed sub-agent's card has the new `--kaboo-error-bg` token behind its
error.

### Markdown

**Who:** apps that restyle `.kaboo-md-li` or `.kaboo-md-spacer`.

Agent text renders as GitHub-flavored markdown with Streamdown, which keeps
text that is still streaming from showing an unclosed `**`. Lists are real
`ul` and `ol` elements, so `.kaboo-md-li` is a list item inside them and
`.kaboo-md-spacer` is gone. To draw agent text with your own renderer instead:

```diff
- <KabooProvider runtimeUrl={url} agent={agent}>
+ <KabooProvider runtimeUrl={url} agent={agent} markdownRenderer={(text) => <MyMarkdown text={text} />}>
```

### New, optional

- **`fallbackToolRenderer`** draws every tool with no renderer of its own, in
  agent timelines and in the chat.
- **`isReadOnlyTool`** folds two or more consecutive reads in an agent's
  timeline into one row ("Read 3 items").
- **`renderAgentResult`** replaces the result area of an agent's card and its
  drill-in view.

## 0.12.1

**Who:** no one needs to change anything.

A sent message renders in CopilotKit's own message and bubble instead of a copy
of its classes, so it follows CopilotKit's styling, and `fast-json-patch` is no
longer installed.

## 0.12

0.12 reads AG-UI's own events: sub-agents as `SUBAGENT_*` events, questions as
tools the browser runs, approvals as native interrupts. Upgrade the three
libraries together: kaboo-workflows 0.29, kaboo-runtime 0.8 and kaboo-react 0.12.
It needs CopilotKit 1.79.1 or later:

```diff
- "@copilotkit/react-core": ">=1.78.0 <2"
+ "@copilotkit/react-core": ">=1.79.1 <2"
```

### Cards come from sub-agent events

**Who:** everyone, and code that reads `useActivity()`.

The groups are folded from `SUBAGENT_*` events and the events tagged with their
`subagentRunId`, live and on replay alike. The entry agent has no group any more
(`inlineChatOwner` is gone): its work is the chat. `StreamGroup.tokens` and the
embedded `tool` on timeline entries are removed — read the timeline's text
entries, and resolve tool entries with `resolveTimelineTool`.
`applyActivityPatch` is removed. `usageByRun` and `traceByRun` now come from
each run's `RUN_FINISHED`, and a group's `traceId` from its `SUBAGENT_STARTED`.

### Questions and requests are tools the browser runs

**Who:** apps with questions, file or data-source requests, or a custom question
card.

Register the tools; an agent calls them when its workflow's `client_tools`
allow it:

```diff
- <KabooProvider ...>  {/* KabooAskUser answered ask_user interrupts */}
+ function BrowserTools() {
+   useAskUserTool();
+   useRequestTool({ name: "request_files", description, parameters, render: FilesPanel });
+   return null;
+ }
```

`KabooAskUser` is removed. A custom question card moves from
`interruptRenderers={{ form: Card }}` to `useAskUserTool({ render: Card })`, and
receives `args`, `status`, `answer` and `skip` instead of `reason`, `onResolve`
and `onCancel`. Pre-0.27 question shapes (`type: "checkbox"`, `input_type`) are no
longer read. See [Human-in-the-loop](hitl.md).

### Approvals render on CopilotKit's `useInterrupt`

**Who:** apps that used the InterruptBridge.

`InterruptBridgeProvider`, `InterruptBridgePublisher`, `useInterruptBridge` and
`useInterruptFor` are removed. `KabooInterruptHandler` draws approvals and your
own interrupt kinds from CopilotKit's `useInterrupt`; `interruptRenderers`,
`approvalScopes` and `onInterruptError` work as before. Continuation pauses are
no longer resolved, because kaboo-workflows 0.29 no longer sends them.

### `KabooProvider` passes generative UI through

**Who:** apps that set CopilotKit props through `copilotKitProps`.

`properties`, `renderToolCalls`, `renderActivityMessages`, `a2ui` and
`openGenerativeUI` are props of `KabooProvider` now:

```diff
- <KabooProvider runtimeUrl="/api/copilotkit" agent="kaboo" copilotKitProps={{ properties }}>
+ <KabooProvider runtimeUrl="/api/copilotkit" agent="kaboo" properties={properties}>
```

### The turn footer renders for every turn

**Who:** apps with a `turnFooter`.

The footer renders after every turn's last reply, including a turn the agent
answered without delegating; its `groups` is empty then. `runIds` lists every run
since the person's message.

### New

- **`KabooChat`** — the chat with kaboo's transcript and drill-down, whose
  composer sends through **`useKabooSend`**, so a new message skips open requests.
- **`useAgentState`, `useLiveToolCalls`, `useAgentPresence`** for canvases
  ([Concepts](concepts.md#shared-state-and-the-canvas)).
- **`withSubagentLabel`** labels a sub-agent's generative UI surface
  ([Generative UI](generative-ui.md)).
- **Tool renderers registered with CopilotKit** draw inside sub-agent cards too
  ([Custom tool cards](tool-cards.md)).
- **Tool labels and structured outputs** from kaboo-workflows 0.29 show on
  sub-agents' cards.
- The package's CommonJS build has its own type declarations.

## 0.11.3

**Who:** apps whose agent delegates to sub-agents that ask questions or need
approvals.

A request a delegate waits on now shows under its card and in its drill-in
view. Upgrade together with kaboo-workflows 0.28.3, which records the
coordinator's own tool calls: without this release, those requests are drawn
nowhere. To let people open a delegate's work, place `GlassTabs` and
`DrillDetailView` beside the chat, as in [Getting started](getting-started.md#add-drill-down).

## 0.11.2

**Who:** apps with approvals or questions, apps that recover from a refused
answer themselves, and apps with a `turnFooter`.

Answers that never reach the agent (the host refuses a decision, or the request
fails) now come back to be answered again, with the reason above them, instead
of staying "Response submitted" until a reload. To show the reason elsewhere
too, pass `onInterruptError`:

```diff
- <KabooProvider runtimeUrl="/api/copilotkit" agent="assistant">
+ <KabooProvider runtimeUrl="/api/copilotkit" agent="assistant" onInterruptError={(message) => toast.error(message)}>
```

If your app reconnected the agent itself after such a failure, remove that
code. Pair this release with kaboo-runtime 0.7.1, which opens a run that fails
before the agent starts with `RUN_STARTED`; older runtimes recover too.

`useInterruptBridge()` also gives `failure`, `setFailure` and `clearAnswered`
for custom cards, and tools still running in a run that errors or stops now
show as cancelled instead of spinning.

With kaboo-workflows 0.28.2, a turn resumed after an answer ends after its last
reply: the `turnFooter` slot renders there, and its new `runIds` list every run
of the turn. If your footer looked things up by the groups' `runId`, use
`runIds` instead; the groups' `runId` is only the run that opened them.

## 0.11

**Who:** everyone. 0.11 runs on CopilotKit 1.78 or later, the AG-UI 1.0
generation.

```diff
- "@copilotkit/react-core": ">=1.62.0 <1.71.2"
+ "@copilotkit/react-core": ">=1.78.0 <2"
```

Upgrade `@copilotkit/react-core` with it, and the server's CopilotKit packages
with kaboo-runtime 0.7. The components and hooks are unchanged. On CopilotKit
1.62 to 1.71.1, stay on kaboo-react 0.10.

## 0.10.1

**Who:** anyone on CopilotKit 1.71.2 or later.

The peer range now stops where this release is tested:

```diff
- "@copilotkit/react-core": ">=1.62.0"
+ "@copilotkit/react-core": ">=1.62.0 <1.71.2"
```

CopilotKit 1.71.2 and later bring in AG-UI 1.0 pieces, which the next minor
release supports. Until then, stay on CopilotKit 1.71.1 or earlier.

## 0.10

### The built-in question card replaces custom clarification panels

**Who:** apps that register their own `form` renderer to get a Cursor-style
question card — kaboo and kaboo-bmo route `ask_user` to a `ClarificationPanel`.

The built-in card is now that card: the agent's options, single or
multi-select, an **Other** row with a text field on every question, Submit and
Skip. Delete the custom panel and style the built-in one with the theme tokens
and class names ([Theming](theming.md#questions-and-approvals)).

```diff
- function KabooFormInterrupt(props: InterruptRendererProps) {
-   // ...file and datasource branches...
-   return (
-     <ClarificationPanel
-       questions={toClarificationQuestions(props.reason)}
-       onSubmit={(answers) => props.onResolve(answersToPayload(props.reason, answers))}
-     />
-   );
- }
- const interruptRenderers = { form: KabooFormInterrupt }
+ // No form renderer: the built-in question card handles ask_user.
```

There is no free-text box any more. A question from an agent before
kaboo-workflows 0.27 with no options is answered through Other alone; one with
`type: "checkbox"` is multi-select.

### Custom request kinds replace `kaboo_kind`

**Who:** apps whose tools disguise a file or data source picker as a text
question with a discriminator (`kind`, `kaboo_kind`) and route it from a `form`
renderer.

Register a renderer per kind instead. The tool raises `type: "files"` (see the
kaboo-workflows [upgrade guide](https://gl-pgege.github.io/kaboo-workflows/upgrading/)),
and its fields arrive on `reason`.

```diff
- if (reason.kaboo_kind === "files") {
-   return <FilePanel context={reason.questions[0]?.question ?? ""} onSubmit={props.onResolve} />;
- }
+ interruptRenderers={{ files: FilesRenderer, datasources: DatasourcesRenderer }}
```

```tsx
import { KabooProvider, type InterruptRendererProps } from "@pgege/kaboo-react";

interface FilesRequest {
  type: string;
  message?: string;
  accept?: string[];
}

function FilesRenderer({ reason, onResolve, onCancel }: InterruptRendererProps<FilesRequest>) {
  return (
    <div>
      <p>{reason.message}</p>
      <input
        type="file"
        accept={reason.accept?.join(",")}
        onChange={(e) => onResolve({ files: [...(e.target.files ?? [])].map((f) => f.name) })}
      />
      <button onClick={onCancel}>Skip</button>
    </div>
  );
}

export function Chat({ threadId }: { threadId: string }) {
  return (
    <KabooProvider
      runtimeUrl="/api/copilotkit"
      agent="kaboo"
      threadId={threadId}
      interruptRenderers={{ files: FilesRenderer }}
    >
      <div />
    </KabooProvider>
  );
}
```

A kind with no registered renderer gets a minimal card with its `message` and
Skip.

### The approval card offers more, and sends more

**Who:** everyone using the built-in approval card, and custom approval
renderers.

- **New options:** Allow for this chat and Always allow appear when the agent
  offers them (kaboo-workflows 0.27 with a host that remembers decisions, or a
  tool that enforces its own approvals); `approvalScopes` on `KabooProvider`
  narrows them for the app. "Applies to …" above them names what they cover
  (`reason.subject.label`).
- **Deny replaces Reject,** with an optional reason. It is sent through
  `onResolve({ status: "cancelled", reason })`, not `onCancel()`. `onCancel()`
  now means skip.
- **Approve sends a scope:** `{ status: "approved", scope: "once" }`.
- **Approve all / Deny all** appear with two or more approvals waiting.
- **Deadlines** are read from `reason.expiresAt` (the request's metadata); an
  expired card offers only Dismiss.
- **Tool-requested approvals** (kaboo-workflows' `interrupt.tool_approvals`)
  render on the same card; `reason.request` carries the tool's request ID for
  the host, and the card needs no change.

Custom approval cards keep these by rendering `ApprovalActions` or using
`useApprovalDecision`:

```diff
  function MyApproval(props: InterruptRendererProps) {
-   return <button onClick={() => props.onResolve({ status: "approved" })}>OK</button>;
+   return <ApprovalActions {...(props as InterruptRendererProps<ApprovalReason>)} />;
  }
```

### Sending a message skips what is waiting

**Who:** everyone; no code change.

Before, a message sent while a question or approval was open was refused by the
AG-UI client and silently lost. Now the handler drops the stale requests just
before the run starts, and the agent closes them as skipped and answers the
message. Remove any composer workaround that blocked sending.

### Types

- `FormQuestion` is `{ question, options, multiple? }`; `type` is deprecated
  and read only when `multiple` is absent. `toFormQuestion` reads either shape.
- `InterruptRendererProps<R>` takes the reason it handles; it defaults to the
  built-in kinds.
- `InterruptRenderers` (and `interruptRenderers`) is keyed by any request kind.
- `ApprovalReason` gains `subject`, `scopes`, `expiresAt` and `request`;
  `ApprovalDecision`, `ApprovalScope`, `ApprovalSubject` and
  `CustomRequestReason` are new.
- `useInterruptBridge()` adds `answered` and `markAnswered`.

### Wording

The answered Q&A card labels a question the person skipped "Skipped" (was
"Declined by user"). `isCancelledResult` recognises the agent's new notes
("Declined", "Skipped", "Expired", "The person skipped this question").

---
